chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Salama ibn al-Khattab al-Barawastani, from Muhammad ibn al-Layth, from Jabir ibn Isma'il, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both):
A man asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) about night prayer (qiyam al-layl) with the Quran. So he said to him: Glad tidings!

Whoever prays one tenth of the night for Allah sincerely, seeking the pleasure of Allah — Allah the Mighty and Majestic says to His angels: 'Record for My servant, among good deeds, a number equal to what grows in the night of seeds, leaves, and trees, and the number of every reed, branch, and pasture.'

Whoever prays one ninth of the night, Allah grants him ten answered supplications and gives him his book in his right hand on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever prays one eighth of the night, Allah gives him the reward of a patient martyr with a sincere intention, and he intercedes for his household. Whoever prays one seventh of the night, he will emerge from his grave on the day of resurrection with his face like the full moon, until he passes over the Bridge with the safe ones.

Whoever prays one sixth of the night, he will be recorded among the repentant (awwabin) and his past sins will be forgiven. Whoever prays one fifth of the night, he will gather with Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful (Khalil al-Rahman), in his dome. Whoever prays one quarter of the night, he will be among the first of the triumphant, until he passes over the Bridge like a raging wind, and he will enter Paradise without reckoning.

Whoever prays one third of the night, not an angel will remain except that it envies him his station with Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and it will be said to him: Enter through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise you wish. Whoever prays half the night — even if he were given the earth's fill of gold seventy thousand times, it would not equal his reward; and that would be greater for him than freeing seventy slaves from the descendants of Isma'il. Whoever prays two thirds of the night, he will have good deeds in the measure of the sands of 'Alij, the least of which is a deed ten times heavier than Mount Uhud.

Whoever prays a full night, reciting the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, bowing, prostrating, and remembering — he is given such reward that the least of it is that he emerges from his sins as his mother bore him; good deeds equal to everything Allah has created are recorded for him, and similar degrees; light is established in his grave; sin and envy are removed from his heart; he is protected from the punishment of the grave; he is given freedom from the Fire; he is raised with the safe ones.

The Lord — Blessed and Exalted — says to His angels: 'My angels! Look at My servant who kept the night alive seeking My pleasure. Settle him in the Highest Paradise (al-Firdaws), and therein he has one hundred thousand cities; in each city is everything that souls desire and eyes delight in, and what no mind can conceive, beyond what I have prepared for him of honor, abundance, and nearness.'

key_terms.ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اللَّهِ: Seeking the pleasure of Allah — the proper intention for worship
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge (al-Sirat) — the path over Hell on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْأَوَّابِينَ: al-Awwabin — those who constantly return to Allah in repentance
key_terms.الْفِرْدَوْس: al-Firdaws — the highest level of Paradise
key_terms.خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَن: Friend of the Merciful — title of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
key_terms.قِيَامُ اللَّيْلِ: Night prayer/vigil (qiyam al-layl) — voluntary nocturnal worship

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for night prayer (qiyam al-layl) according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about night prayer with Quran recitation, and he responded with a comprehensive description of the graduated rewards for praying different fractions of the night — from one tenth up to the full night. This teaching, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq and al-Baqir, was delivered in response to a specific question, addressing the audience's practical concern about the spiritual benefits of night worship. The framing as graduated rewards reflects the pedagogical style of the Imams, encouraging incremental practice and emphasizing that even partial night prayer carries immense divine reward.
